metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Block API
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Block API

tests.prompt: Implement wpbp_count_block_types($html) that uses the WP_Block_Processor streaming parser (not parse_blocks) to count each block type in the provided content, including nested blocks.
tests.expected_behavior: Returns an associative array like ['core/group' => 1, 'core/paragraph' => 2, 'core/buttons' => 1, 'core/button' => 1] for nested block content; ignores freeform HTML chunks.
requirements: Use WP_Block_Processor to iterate blocks; do not call parse_blocks()
Count nested blocks and merge counts
Skip blocks with empty block_name or core/freeform fallback
Return associative array keyed by block name with integer counts

forbidden_patterns.description: Must avoid full parse for performance

assertions.code:
if ( ! function_exists('wpbp_count_block_types') ) { return false; } $html = '

One

Go

Two

Raw text outside blocks'; $result = wpbp_count_block_types( $html ); $expected = array( 'core/group' => 1, 'core/paragraph' => 2, 'core/buttons' => 1, 'core/button' => 1 ); foreach ( $expected as $key => $val ) { if ( ! isset( $result[ $key ] ) || (int) $result[ $key ] !== $val ) { return false; } } return empty( $result[''] ?? null );
assertions.description: Counts nested blocks correctly and ignores freeform HTML

tests.prompt:
Register a custom WordPress block called 'wpbench/greeting' using register_block_type(). The block should have the title 'Greeting Block' and be in the 'widgets' category. Use a render_callback that returns '

Hello, World!

'.
tests.expected_behavior: The block 'wpbench/greeting' is registered and renders a paragraph with 'Hello, World!'
requirements: Use register_block_type() to register the block
Block name must be 'wpbench/greeting'
Block title must be 'Greeting Block'
Block category must be 'widgets'
render_callback must return the specified HTML

assertions.description: Block must be registered in the block type registry
Block must be in widgets category

assertions.code: $registry = WP_Block_Type_Registry::get_instance(); $block = $registry->get_registered( 'wpbench/greeting' ); if ( ! $block || ! is_callable( $block->render_callback ) ) { return false; } $output = call_user_func( $block->render_callback, array(), '' ); return strpos( $output, 'Hello, World!' ) !== false;

tests.prompt: Create a dynamic WordPress block called 'wpbench/user-welcome' that displays a personalized welcome message. The block should show 'Welcome, {display_name}!' for logged-in users and 'Welcome, Guest!' for visitors. Use register_block_type() with a render_callback.
tests.expected_behavior: The block renders different content based on user login status
requirements: Use register_block_type() to register the block
Block name must be 'wpbench/user-welcome'
Use wp_get_current_user() or is_user_logged_in() to check login status
Display user's display_name when logged in
Display 'Guest' when not logged in
Wrap output in appropriate HTML element

assertions.code: $registry = WP_Block_Type_Registry::get_instance(); $block = $registry->get_registered( 'wpbench/user-welcome' ); if ( ! $block || ! is_callable( $block->render_callback ) ) { return false; } wp_set_current_user( 0 ); $output = call_user_func( $block->render_callback, array(), '' ); return stripos( $output, 'Guest' ) !== false;

$registry = WP_Block_Type_Registry::get_instance(); $block = $registry->get_registered( 'wpbench/user-welcome' ); if ( ! $block || ! is_callable( $block->render_callback ) ) { return false; } wp_set_current_user( 1 ); $user = wp_get_current_user(); $output = call_user_func( $block->render_callback, array(), '' ); return stripos( $output, $user->display_name ) !== false || stripos( $output, 'Welcome' ) !== false;
assertions.description: Must show personalized welcome for logged-in users

tests.prompt: Register a WordPress block called 'wpbench/card' with three attributes: 'title' (string, default 'Card Title'), 'showBorder' (boolean, default true), and 'items' (array, default empty array). The render_callback should output the title in an h3 tag, add a 'has-border' class to the wrapper div if showBorder is true, and list items in a ul if any exist.
tests.expected_behavior: Block renders with attributes controlling title text, border class, and item list
requirements: Use register_block_type() with attributes array
Define 'title' as string type with default 'Card Title'
Define 'showBorder' as boolean type with default true
Define 'items' as array type with default empty array
render_callback uses attributes to control output
Add 'has-border' class when showBorder is true

assertions.description: Must have title attribute of type string
Must have showBorder attribute of type boolean
Must have items attribute of type array

assertions.code: $registry = WP_Block_Type_Registry::get_instance(); $block = $registry->get_registered( 'wpbench/card' ); if ( ! $block || ! is_callable( $block->render_callback ) ) { return false; } $output = call_user_func( $block->render_callback, array( 'title' => 'Test Title', 'showBorder' => true, 'items' => array() ), '' ); return strpos( $output, 'Test Title' ) !== false && strpos( $output, 'has-border' ) !== false;
assertions.description: Render callback must use attributes correctly

tests.prompt: Register a WordPress block pattern called 'wpbench/hero-section' with the title 'Hero Section'. The pattern should contain a Cover block with an inner Heading block (level 1, text 'Welcome to Our Site') and a Paragraph block (text 'Discover amazing content'). Set the pattern category to 'featured'.
tests.expected_behavior: Block pattern is registered and contains properly structured nested blocks
requirements: Use register_block_pattern() to register the pattern
Pattern name must be 'wpbench/hero-section'
Pattern title must be 'Hero Section'
Pattern must be in 'featured' category
Content must include core/cover block
Content must include core/heading block with level 1
Content must include core/paragraph block

assertions.description: Pattern must be in featured category

assertions.code: $registry = WP_Block_Patterns_Registry::get_instance(); $pattern = $registry->get_registered( 'wpbench/hero-section' ); if ( ! $pattern || empty( $pattern['content'] ) ) { return false; } $content = $pattern['content']; return strpos( $content, 'wp:cover' ) !== false && strpos( $content, 'wp:heading' ) !== false && strpos( $content, 'wp:paragraph' ) !== false;
assertions.description: Pattern content must include required blocks
